request.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates programming worked examples into other natural languages, maintaining both technical accuracy and the original code formatting.

[[TASK-DEFINITION]] You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]. [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Calculating and Rounding Up Body Mass Index (BMI) To the Nearest Integer [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] BMI is a measure of body fat based on height and weight that applies to adult men and women. BMI Categories are as follows: \nUnderweight = <18.5\nNormal weight = 18.5–24.9\nOverweight = 25–29.9\nObesity = BMI of 30 or greater.\nEnglish BMI Formula (Imperial) is: BMI = (Weight in Pounds / (Height in inches x Height in inches)) x 703.\n BMI results are usually displayed as integers (values without decimal points). Construct a program to round the BMI result to the nearest integer. [[SOURCE-CODE]] [[LINE01]] #Step 1: Receive the weight and height from the user [[LINE02]] text = input("Enter the weight in pounds:") [[LINE03]] weight = float(text) [[LINE04]] text = input("Enter the height in inches:") [[LINE05]] height = float(text) [[LINE06]] #Step 2: Calculate BMI [[LINE07]] bmi = weight / height ** 2 * 703 [[LINE08]] #Step 3: Round up BMI [[LINE09]] bmi = round(bmi) [[LINE10]] #Step 4: Print results [[LINE11]] print("The BMI rounded to the nearest integer is:", bmi) [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the weight in pounds, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string. [[LINE03.EXPL1]] We need to convert the input text to its float representation because weight could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float(). [[LINE03.EXPL2]] Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value. [[LINE04.EXPL1]] We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter height in inches, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string. [[LINE05.EXPL1]] We need to convert the input text to its float representation because height could have a decimal point. For this purpose, we use the conversion function float(). [[LINE05.EXPL2]] Note that this can only be done if user input could be translated into a valid floating-point value. [[LINE07.EXPL1]] We calculate the BMI using the mathematical expression in this statement. [[LINE07.EXPL2]] The height ** 2 returns the value of height raised to the power of the 2. Note that the ** operator is the exponent operator. [[LINE07.EXPL3]] Note that the exponent (**) has the highest precedence level so it's the first operation that is performed. Also, multiplication (*) and division operator (/) are in the same precedence level, and thus, are evaluated from left to right in this expression. Therefore, we don't need to enclose the division operator and its operands in parentheses. [[LINE09.EXPL1]] We round up the BMI to the nearest integer. For this purpose we use the round() function. [[LINE09.EXPL2]] Note that, by default, this function rounds the number to 0 digits from the decimal point. Since we want to round BMI to the nearest integer, we need to use round(bmi [[LINE11.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "The BMI rounded to the nearest integer is:" and the value of variable bmi.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]] [[DIST1.LC]] bmi = int(bmi) [[DIST2.LC]] bmi = round(bmi,2) [[DIST3.LC]] bmi = float(bmi) [[DIST4.LC]] bmi = round(bmi,1) [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]] Translate the given worked example into Arabic. Be sure to specifically translate the sections labeled [[PROGRAM-NAME]], [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]], [[SOURCE-CODE]], [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]], and [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters). Preserve the original format and Do NOT add, remove, or change any content beyond translation.
